title: Aqualung
summary: This file gathers the lyrics of several Jethro Tull albums, presented as a plain-text archive from a fan lyrics site rather than a prose book. The first section is the lyric sheet for Aqualung (1971), a concept-flavoured rock album whose title song follows a destitute, dishevelled old man on a park bench, with other pieces such as Cross-Eyed Mary, Locomotive Breath, Hymn 43 and My God turning a satirical eye on religion, class, wealth and institutions. A second section covers Catfish Rising (1991), a set of songs on urban alienation, drifting relationships and modern consumer life, including Rocks on the Road, Sparrow on the Schoolyard Wall and Doctor to My Disease. A third portion reproduces the lyrics of Thick as a Brick (1972), a single long composition split into two parts, mock-epic in tone, satirising childhood, war and cultural pretension. The excerpts also include the closing material of a later album, with songs such as Paparazzi and Apogee. Each album lists its musicians and track titles in the archive.
